subject: Priority routing & reliability crediting — commercial proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Evan Rossi <evan.rossi@brightline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority routing / reliability credits — initial ask

Thanks Kimberly / Jonas — quick note from our side after the demo last week. Brightline wants a commercial approach that guarantees predictable behavior during cross-region degradations. Two asks: 1) a way to prioritize our traffic (we're calling it "priority routing") that survives regional failover, and 2) a reliability-crediting mechanism if availability drops below the agreed band.

Specifically:
- Priority routing: we'd like a hard flag so critical requests route to dedicated pools (or the lowest-latency fallback) with observable metrics.
- Reliability credits: a simple credit schedule that scales with observed downtime (credits applied as service usage credits).

Could you send a short proposal that maps pricing to these two items? Procurement would also like to know whether credits will be capped and how they interact with committed capacity.

Appreciate it — Evan

--
Evan Rossi

Subject: Re: Priority routing / reliability credits — initial ask

Evan — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short commercial sketch (redwood-pricing-prc-model.xlsx) and a draft SOW that maps the options to tiers. High level summary here:

1) Priority Routing (we call it "Priority Routing Credits" or PRCs)
- PRC basics: token-based prioritization. Customers buy a PRC pool attached to a commit; each prioritized request consumes from the PRC pool.
- Routing guarantee: PRC requests are routed ahead of standard traffic within the same commit pool; if the local region is degraded we route to your reserved failover pool or to Redwood Dedicated within the same region family.
- Pricing: PRCs sold as monthly bundles (e.g., 50k PRCs for $X, 250k PRCs for $Y). Unused PRCs roll over for one billing cycle.

2) Reliability credit schedule
- Uptime bands: >= 99.95% (no credits), 99.9–99.95% (tier 1 credit), 99.5–99.9% (tier 2 credit), <99.5% (tier 3 credit). Credits issued as a % of monthly committed fees and capped at 30% per month.
- Interaction with commit: credits apply to committed spend only; overage charges are not eligible.
- Measurement window & proof: we use per-route availability aggregates (your PRC-tagged routes included). Credits are issued after joint verification; typical cadence is within 30 days post-incident.

3) Operational coverage & escalation
- Included: 24/7 paging for P1 incidents during your committed SLA hours, with a named oncall contact.
- Optional: 24/7 L2 coverage add-on (flat monthly fee) that includes oncall overlap and playbook-driven runbooks.

I've pulled in Jonas and Marissa for technical and commercial sizing commentary. If this looks directionally right I'll push a quantitative price table and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-prc-model.xlsx, Brightline_SOW_draft_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Evan Rossi <evan.rossi@brightline.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priority routing / reliability credits — initial ask

Kimberly — a few clarifying points I highlighted in the attached tab (see pricing workbook):
- PRC burn model: PRCs should prioritize by request class (critical vs normal). We recommend a lightweight header on requests so PRC consumption is deterministic.
- Failover behavior: PRCs move with the logical route — if Brightline opts into multi-region failover we provision a soft-reserve in the adjacent region to avoid cold-start impact. That reserve increases the effective committed spend a bit; pricing table reflects both "single-region" and "multi-region reserve" lines.
- Credits cap & stacking: credits are per-commit and capped as Kimberly noted. One nuance: if a credit is issued during a trial month we'll apply the monetary credit to the next invoice rather than reducing historical committed usage.

Evan — two quick operational asks for procurement: can you confirm which routes will be PRC-tagged (e.g., inference-api/v1/generate vs embedding routes)? That determines bucket sizing.

-Jonas

Thanks everyone — procurement had two constraints: 1) any credit mechanism must be predictable and not overly discretionary (they want clear triggers & math), and 2) they'd like a short introductory concession: a 10% credit on PRC bundles for the first 90 days as a trial incentive.

On triggers & math: they want a simple table that maps minutes of unavailability per month to credit %. The schedule you proposed looks fine, but procurement asked that we add a small escalator at the high end (e.g., if downtime > 12h in a month, increase the credit by an additional 5%).

About routes: we'll tag these routes initially: /api/v1/generate (chat/generation), /api/v1/embeddings (batch embedding jobs). We expect ~60% PRC consumption on generate traffic at launch.

If you can share a DocuSign-ready SOW and a final PRC price table (with the 90-day promo line), procurement is ready to review and fast-track.

Best,
Evan

Evan — great, thanks for the clarity. Action items and decisions captured below so procurement can move: 

1) Pricing & promo: we will include a 90-day introductory PRC promo at 10% off the published bundle price. After the promo window pricing reverts to standard PRC rates.
2) Credit escalator: agreed — add an escalator so credits increase by +5% if monthly unavailability exceeds 12 hours. We'll add that row to the credit table.
3) Measurement & payout: credits calculated monthly on PRC-tagged routes and applied to the next invoice (per Jonas' note). Joint verification window = 30 days after the end of the month.
4) DocuSign & SOW: I'll update the SOW with the promo clauses and escalator, then push a DocuSign packet (will include the HubSpot deal link you noted). Expect SOW v3 -> v4 with redline margin changes by tomorrow EOD.

Next steps (owner):
- Kimberly: finalize price table + SOW v4 & send DocuSign (ETA: 2026-10-16 18:00 UTC).
- Jonas: confirm technical addendum re: multi-region soft-reserve (ETA: same).
- Evan/procurement: confirm route list is final and share billing contact.

If procurement wants any additional guardrails (e.g., max monthly credit floor), flag them and we'll incorporate.
